BEH-CO-01.text: **Golden harness.** `hub golden-compare` replays the Stage 7 capture scenarios (CT-01..CT-16) against the new modules' preserved functions and the legacy code through read-only adapters, and prints every difference as `{golden_ref, legacy, new, disposition}` where disposition is `identical`, `approved_deviation(<dev_id>, <HAR-06 reference>)` or `UNAPPROVED`. Exit code non-zero if any `UNAPPROVED`.

BEH-CO-02.text: **Deviation register.** `deviation_register` rows `{dev_id, golden_ref, legacy_value, new_value, justification, approval_ref, status}`; `status` in {proposed, approved, rejected}. Only `approved` with a non-empty `approval_ref` counts as approved; DV-01..DV-09 ship `proposed`. Approval is recorded by Dinesh Naik outside the product and referenced.

BEH-CO-03.text: **Read-only legacy.** C11 opens legacy databases only with `file:<path>?mode=ro` (immutable where the file is a baseline); no new-module code writes under legacy paths; legacy source files (`app/`, `legacy_js/`, `legacy_batch/`, `legacy_java/`, `sql/`, `contracts/`) are unmodified in R1 (git diff on those paths is empty).

BEH-CO-04.text: **Sandbox guard.** The harness and acceptance suite refuse to run when the working data directory resolves inside the original repository root (E-CO-NOT-SANDBOX) and verify the backup manifest before and after (`sha256sum -c --quiet ../_data-backup-2026-10-17/SHA256SUMS.txt`).

BEH-CO-05.text: **Protected parallel workflow.** `coexistence_inventory` lists protected workflows `{item_id, description, owner, status}`; the older-customer parallel workflow is item CO-WF-01 with `owner = Unknown`. The product exposes it read-only; no endpoint, job or rule can alter, disable or retire it.

BEH-CO-06.text: **Rollback.** Each release has a rollback procedure document and a rehearsal record: stop process, restore `hub.sqlite3` + anchor file from the pre-release backup, verify checksum and audit chain, restart. Replay-safety (G2) must pass before the release is marked ready.

BEH-CO-07.text: **No-AI enforcement.** CI blocks any dependency or import from the deny-list (openai, anthropic, transformers, torch, langchain, llama, sklearn and any HTTP client outside `adapters/`); the process makes no outbound connection except the loopback gateway (egress test with sockets patched); `model_calls_total` metric is emitted and equals 0. Adding any AI element requires a new Stage 8 qualification and Dinesh's decision. AI coding assistants used to build the product are out of scope of this rule (BR-AI-7).

BEH-CO-08.text: **Determinism.** Core paths (decision fold, rule evaluation, intake classification, metrics) use no `random`, no wall-clock inside pure functions (time injected), stable ordering, and produce bit-identical output across `PYTHONHASHSEED`, timezone and locale.

BEH-CO-09.text: **Runtime floor.** New code uses only features available in Python 3.10 and SQLite 3.37 until the target runtime is confirmed (ADR-018 says 3.12; `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python >= 3.10` and no dependencies; dev device is 3.10.12); the start-up self-check prints Python, SQLite and FTS5 versions.

BEH-DEC-01.text: Every state change or decision is stored by `DecisionService.append()` as one new row in `decision_events` (schema SCH-DEC-EVENT). The service exposes NO update or delete method. Database triggers reject `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on `decision_events` with error E-DEC-IMMUTABLE. `seq` is gapless and strictly increasing per `case_id`, starting at 1.

BEH-DEC-02.text: A `CASE_CREATED` event records `from_state = null` and `to_state` = the state **at creation** (never the current state). Legacy cases are brought in by the legacy adapter (C11) as `CASE_IMPORTED` events with `basis = "legacy snapshot"`, `actor_kind = system`, `to_state` = snapshot status; no history is invented.

BEH-DEC-03.text: Current state of a case = `to_state` of its highest-`seq` event with `affects_state = true`. A materialised projection `case_state` exists for speed and is rebuildable from events; `verify-projection` recomputes every case and reports mismatches.

BEH-DEC-04.text: `GET state?as_of=T` returns the state from the last state-affecting event with `occurred_at <= T` (ties broken by `seq`). If T precedes the first event the response is E-DEC-NOT-YET-EXISTS. `recorded_at` is assigned by the server in UTC; the client may supply `occurred_at` only if `occurred_at <= recorded_at` and `>=` the previous event's `occurred_at` (else E-DEC-TIME-ORDER).

BEH-DEC-05.text: Entering a state whose vocabulary role tag is `reopened` (legacy label REOPENED) is accepted only with `event_type = REOPEN` and a non-empty `basis`; any other event type targeting it is refused (E-DEC-REOPEN-EXPLICIT). A REOPEN increments the case `cycle` counter (cycle starts at 1).

BEH-DEC-06.text: Evidence is attached as its own immutable `EVIDENCE_ATTACHED` event (evidence record `ev_id`, kind in {document, intake_item, crosswalk_object, external_ref}, `source`, `source_hash`). A decision event lists `evidence_refs[]` of existing `ev_id` values. Retrieval (`OP-DEC-04`) returns the event plus each resolved evidence record and its source; a reference that cannot be resolved is returned flagged `unresolvable`, never silently omitted. Evidence the caller may not read (access level, tenant) is returned as a redacted placeholder `{ev_id, access: "denied"}`.

BEH-DEC-07.text: Closing check: for a transition into a closing state (set determined by SBR-DEC-03), require `evidence_refs` with >= 1 resolvable `ev_id` OR a `close_exception` object `{actor, authority, reason}`. Evidence **sufficiency is never judged** (OD-S12-07). Without either: E-DEC-EVIDENCE-REQUIRED. A `close_exception` is a Zone H action (F02): accepted only from an authenticated human holder; otherwise E-GATE-NOT-AUTHORISED. An accepted exception sets `exception = true` on the event and surfaces it in the exception report.

BEH-DEC-08.text: Three separate fact events, each its own event type and none changing state: `FACT_RECEIVED` (written when a case is created via intake; for imported legacy cases `occurred_at = cases.created_at` as proxy - Assumption A-12-F01-1), `FACT_OPS_CLOSED`, `FACT_EVIDENCE_COMPLETE`. Each carries `cycle`. They are recorded by explicit calls from roles reviewer, quality_lead or compliance (OD-S12-15 asks whether a rule may derive them). The system never labels a case 'closed' on the basis of a fact event.

BEH-DEC-09.text: Optimistic concurrency: write requests carry `expected_seq`; mismatch gives E-DEC-SEQ-CONFLICT (409). Writes accept an `Idempotency-Key`; same key + same canonical body returns the original result, same key + different body gives E-DEC-IDEMPOTENCY-MISMATCH (422).

BEH-DEC-10.text: Transition legality is data (`transition_rule`). Shipped default `structural` mode: any change to a different state of the same vocabulary is permitted unless it is Zone H; a same-state request is refused (E-DEC-NOOP). A strict table may be loaded instead (OD-S12-16). Cross-vocabulary mapping is never automatic (knowledge-model K2).

BEH-DEC-11.text: Every append calls the audit chain (ADR-005, F09) in the same database transaction; if the audit write fails the append aborts (component-model dependency rule 5).

BEH-DEC-12.text: Free-text fields (`basis`, `note`) are typed Untrusted: stored verbatim, escaped on output, length-bounded (basis <= 2000 chars), never parsed for commands or state words.

BEH-GATE-01.text: **Non-bypassable human gate.** Zone H actions are executable only through `GateService`. `GateService` accepts a request only if (a) the session is an authenticated interactive human session (`actor_kind = human`), (b) the principal is in `zone_h.holders` with role `dispositioner`, and (c) the step-up re-authentication happened within `zone_h.reauth_window_seconds` (proposed default 300; Assumption). There is no configuration flag, environment variable, debug mode, admin override or batch/CLI path that skips (a)-(c). The check is in the service layer (not HTTP only) and is mirrored by a database trigger that aborts insertion of any Zone H event type unless `actor_kind = 'human'` and a `holder_check_ref` is present.

BEH-GATE-02.text: **No automation path.** Modules C6 (intake), C8 (runs), C9 (metrics), C10 (reviewer support) and C4 (rules) have no import path to `GateService` write methods (static import-graph test, extends CT-16). Reports, templates, rule outputs and search results never contain a pre-filled or pre-selected disposition value. No inbound string (feed `state = DISPOSITIONED`, document text) can create a Zone H event (F04).

BEH-GATE-03.text: **Evidence pack** (`OP-GATE-01`): read-only assembly for one case: case header, state history, linked objects (crosswalk, including 'none found' lists), evidence records with source, rule traces, open findings, overridden flags, current policy versions and active rule set. Output has a deterministic `pack_hash` (sha256 over canonical JSON). The pack never summarises or recommends.

BEH-GATE-04.text: **Pack acknowledgement.** A disposition request must carry the `pack_hash` of the pack the human viewed; if the underlying data changed, the request is refused (E-GATE-PACK-STALE) and the pack must be re-read. [Inference: proposed control so the human decides on current evidence.]

BEH-GATE-05.text: **Holder list ships empty.** `zone_h.holders` default is `[]`. While empty every Zone H action returns E-GATE-NO-HOLDERS (HTTP 423); no default holder, bootstrap account or first-user-wins rule exists. Holder-list changes are configuration; the hash of the loaded configuration is written to the audit chain at start-up so a change is detectable (OD-S12-06).

BEH-GATE-06.text: **Recording modes** (`disposition.mode`, default `none`): `none` - ZH-01..ZH-03 return E-GATE-MODE-NONE. `event` - the human's decision is stored as a `DISPOSITION_RECORDED` decision event (actor, `decision` from `disposition.values`, basis, evidence refs, `pack_hash`, `mode_at_write`). `external_ref` - only a `DISPOSITION_REFERENCED` event is stored: `{system, reference, uri?, decided_at, decided_by_declared, entered_by, verified: false}`; the hub neither stores the decision content nor verifies the external record. `disposition.values` ships empty and must be set (Zone H, ZH-08) before `event` mode accepts a decision (E-GATE-VALUES-UNSET). Past events keep their `mode_at_write`; switching mode never rewrites them. Both modes are specified and tested; the choice is OD-S12-05.

BEH-GATE-07.text: **Rejected actors.** Service accounts, `integration` role, scheduler/run identities, importer, and any session lacking a human interactive login are rejected with E-GATE-NOT-AUTHORISED and the rejection is written to the audit chain (F09) including actor, action code and correlation id.

BEH-GATE-08.text: **Override, dismiss, refuse.** Every rule-generated item (flag, classification, priority, queue assignment) has a `flag_id`. `OP-GATE-04` accepts `action` in {override, dismiss, refuse}, a non-empty `reason`, and optional `replacement`. The call is permitted to roles reviewer, quality_lead, compliance; the system never blocks it for any reason except missing reason (E-GATE-REASON-REQUIRED) or missing authentication. The original rule output is preserved; an `OVERRIDE_RECORDED` event links to it. An override is not a Zone H action and cannot itself produce a disposition.

BEH-ID-01.text: **Link record** (SCH-CROSSWALK): `link_id`, `from_type`, `from_id`, `to_type`, `to_id`, `key_used`, `creator_kind` in {rule, human}, `creator` (rule id or user id), `created_at`, `reason` (required for human), `run_id` (for rule). Links are append-only; removal is a `LINK_RETRACTED` event referencing `link_id` with reason; the current link set is the set of non-retracted links.

BEH-ID-02.text: **Rule links only by exact registered key.** A rule creates a link only if the registered key values are equal as strings after Unicode NFC and trim, and the target resolves to exactly one entity. No prefix, case-folding, edit-distance, token or similarity matching exists in the code (the deny-list test forbids `difflib`, `fuzzy`, `levenshtein` imports in the crosswalk module).

BEH-ID-03.text: **Orphans stay orphans.** An item with no registered-key match remains unlinked in every run; orphan counts per source are a reported measure (DQ-24, FR-MET-07), never an error to repair. Re-running the matcher after more data arrives may create a new rule link only through an exact key.

BEH-ID-04.text: **Human link.** `OP-ID-02` lets roles reviewer, quality_lead, compliance create a link of a registered pair (LT-06 pairs included) with a non-empty `reason`; stored with `creator_kind = human` and an event `LINK_CREATED_HUMAN` (actor, time, reason). A duplicate active link is refused (E-ID-LINK-EXISTS); an unregistered type pair is refused (E-ID-PAIR-NOT-REGISTERED); self-links are refused. Service/integration actors cannot create human links (E-AUTH-FORBIDDEN).

BEH-ID-05.text: **Lookup.** `OP-ID-01` accepts `id` and optional `id_type`. If `id_type` is absent the id is compared with registered id patterns (case `C\d{8}`, batch `BT\d{8}`, others registered); a string matching several patterns returns the candidates and requires `id_type` (E-ID-AMBIGUOUS-TYPE) - no guessing. Response lists direct links with key, creator, time.

BEH-ID-06.text: **(R2) Joined view.** `OP-ID-04` returns the connected set of entities over active links (breadth-first, depth cap 4, size cap 500, `truncated` flag and count when capped), read-only, deterministic order (type, id). Entering with any member id returns the same set. Fields are filtered by caller role/tenant/access level first (F09).

BEH-ID-07.text: **(R2) Consistency findings.** `CONSISTENCY` policy objects (F03) define pairs of conditions over linked entities (e.g. `case.state in {X}` with `batch.qa_status in {Y}`). The check writes `finding` rows `{rule_ref, object_refs, detected_at, policy_version}` idempotently (one open finding per rule+objects+version), changes no state, and never auto-corrects. No CONSISTENCY policy ships adopted, so a fresh install yields zero findings.

BEH-ID-08.text: **Vocabularies are not mapped.** The word CLOSED in cases, batch QA, deviations and enterprise tables is not treated as equivalent; consistency rules compare per-vocabulary values explicitly.

BEH-INT-01.text: **Receive.** Every delivered item gets a new `raw_intake` row (SCH-RAW-INTAKE): `raw_id`, `source`, `source_key` (e.g. feed_id), `partner`, `schema_rev`, `receipt_time` (server UTC), `content_hash`, `identity_key`, `raw_bytes` verbatim, `run_id`. UPDATE/DELETE are rejected by trigger (E-INT-RAW-IMMUTABLE). Processing results go only to the separate append-only `intake_outcome` table (SCH-INTAKE-OUTCOME); the current outcome is the row with the highest `outcome_seq` per `raw_id`. Raw count always equals received count. The legacy `partner_feeds.processing_status` is never read as truth or written.

BEH-INT-02.text: **Identity and hash.** `identity_key` = sha256 of canonical `[source, partner, record_kind, ref_id, source_ts]` (SBR-INT-01). `content_hash` = sha256 of the canonical form (UTF-8, JSON with sorted keys and no insignificant whitespace; for CSV the header-keyed row) of `{schema_rev, payload}`; transport fields (`feed_id`, `ingest_ts`, `processing_status`, `error_reason`) are excluded.

BEH-INT-03.text: **Identical re-delivery.** A new item whose `identity_key` and `content_hash` equal those of an already-received item gets a raw row (`duplicate_of = first raw_id`) and outcome `NOOP_DUPLICATE`, `counts_toward_totals = false`. Queues, queue ages, totals and metrics are computed excluding `NOOP_DUPLICATE`, so replaying changes none of them.

BEH-INT-04.text: **Changed re-delivery.** Same `identity_key`, different `content_hash`: outcome `QUARANTINED`, reason `REVISED_CONFLICT`, queue `revision_review`; both versions stay stored and linked (`conflicts_with`). It is never discarded and never auto-classified as duplicate. A human (reviewer or quality_lead) resolves it with `accept_revision`, `keep_original` or `reject_both` plus a reason; resolution is an event and does not change any case decision.

BEH-INT-05.text: **Validation, three layers.** L1 envelope (DC-01): required `feed_id, partner, schema_rev, source_ts (ISO-8601 UTC), ref_id, record_kind, raw_json`; `schema_rev` in {1.0, 1.1, 2.0} else `UNSUPPORTED_REVISION`; `record_kind` in {OOS_RESULT, DEVIATION, CAPA_UPDATE} else `UNKNOWN_RECORD_KIND`. L2 payload (DC-02): valid JSON object else `INVALID_JSON`; required `object_type, state, source_version` else `MISSING_PAYLOAD_FIELD`; `business_key` absent -> `NO_BUSINESS_KEY`; `quantity` numeric (Decimal) negative -> `NEGATIVE_VALUE`, non-numeric -> `UNPARSABLE_AMOUNT`; `unit` outside {lb, kg, hour, each, percent, ppm} -> `UNKNOWN_UNIT`; `currency` not ISO-4217 shaped (3 upper letters) or outside {USD, GBP, INR, JPY, EUR} -> `UNKNOWN_CURRENCY` (closed sets are Assumptions). L3 declared contract: see BEH-INT-06. Invalid items are stored in quarantine with a reason code, never merely counted.

BEH-INT-06.text: **Declared contract binding.** `contract_binding(source -> contract_file, mode)`, `mode` in {`enforce`, `record_only`}. Default for every source is `record_only` until OD-S12-11 is decided: the L3 check runs and its result (`contract_check` in {pass, fail, not_bound}, missing keys) is stored on the outcome, but a failure alone does not quarantine. With `mode = enforce` a failure gives `CONTRACT_VIOLATION` and quarantine. Changing a binding is Zone H-classified configuration (ZH-10). Expected effect of `enforce` on the baseline: partner_feeds 8,567/8,567 quarantined; source_messages 0/15; gateway_inbox 1/1.

BEH-INT-07.text: **Classification** is a pure deterministic function of (item, validation config version). Every non-clean outcome has one `primary_reason` chosen by the fixed precedence in SBR-INT-03 plus the full `all_reasons[]` and exactly one queue (reason-code catalogue in schema-specifications.md SCH-REASON). Same input and config give the same codes. No randomness, no model.

BEH-INT-08.text: **Match** (after validation) via the crosswalk (F05): exact string equality of the item `ref_id` against the configured keys of core entities, in configured order. Exactly one hit -> `crosswalk_link(creator=rule)` created and the item shown to reviewers as matched; zero -> outcome reason `UNMATCHED_REF`, queue `unmatched`; more than one -> `AMBIGUOUS_MATCH`, queue `ambiguous_match`, candidates listed, **no link created**. No normalisation beyond Unicode NFC and trim; no similarity. Baseline expectation: 173 of 8,567 feed `ref_id` equal a `cases.id`; 8,394 unmatched (DQ-06).

BEH-INT-09.text: **Untrusted text.** All free-text fields (feed `notes`, document bodies, e-mail bodies, gateway/CSV payload text) are typed `Untrusted`. The type cannot be passed to any decision, status, priority, queue, approval or disposition parameter (static type-check test + runtime guard raising E-INT-UNTRUSTED-USE). Also payload fields such as `state`, `quality_flag`, `subtype` are stored as `source_*` attributes and never mapped to case status. Output is HTML-escaped, length-bounded for display and marked 'untrusted source text'.

BEH-INT-10.text: **Adapters and backfill.** Legacy tables are read via C11 with `file:...?mode=ro`; backfill of the 8,567 feed rows into `raw_intake` is idempotent by `content_hash` + `identity_key`, uses `receipt_time = ingest_ts` as a proxy (Assumption A-12-F04-1) and never writes to legacy.

BEH-INT-11.text: **Gateway and file sources.** Gateway reads accept only `http`/`https` URLs resolving to loopback (rejecting `file:`, `ftp:` - DM-15), 5 s timeout, bounded retry (`gateway.retries`, default 3, exponential back-off); unreachable source is a run error, not a data outcome (F06). Invalid gateway events are stored in quarantine (DC-04). Vendor CSV is parsed by header names (never position), `amount` kept as text plus Decimal, unparsable -> `UNPARSABLE_AMOUNT` (never skipped), identifier pattern `GXP-########` mismatch (all 2,400 `GXP--`) -> flag `IDENTIFIER_PATTERN` with original preserved.

BEH-INT-12.text: **Delay, missing, revised (R2).** For each source the system computes `delay = receipt_time - source_ts` (negative values flagged `FUTURE_SOURCE_TS`; 2,234 of 8,567 rows have source_ts > ingest_ts today) and lists items by source and time without manual spreadsheet work. Thresholds are configuration (PNFR-03/04 are Assumptions).

BEH-MET-01.text: **Metric registry.** Every metric is declared in `metric_definition` (SCH-METRIC-DEF): `metric_id`, `name`, `category` in {time, count, money, rate, age}, `definition_tag` (required, non-null, when the figure involves closed, resolved, approved, cost or handling time), `window`, `denominator`, `exclusions`, `cutoff_ref`, `basis` in {event_derived, modelled}, documentation text. A metric whose category involves those concepts but whose tag is null cannot be registered (E-MET-TAG-REQUIRED); a release test enumerates the registry.

BEH-MET-02.text: **Metric value** (SCH-METRIC-VALUE) always carries `definition_tag`, `policy_version` (of the policy object supplying the tag; 'candidate' status shown), window, denominator, exclusions, `n`, `basis`, `inputs_hash`, `code_version`, `computed_at` and the label **'synthetic, unvalidated'** while the data is synthetic (flag `data_origin = synthetic`, set by configuration and not removable per figure). Every rendering (API, HTML, CSV export, report) shows tag, policy version and label.

BEH-MET-03.text: **No mixing.** The only arithmetic/comparison entry points are `combine(values, op)` and `compare(a, b)`. If the inputs carry different `definition_tag` (or different policy versions of the same tag) they raise E-MET-TAG-MIX. Tables may show different tags only through `side_by_side()`, which requires one labelled column per tag, performs no sum/ratio/difference across columns and prints 'different definitions - not comparable'. A report that claims improvement under one tag while another tag worsens carries the flag `FAIL-02-conflict` (OPD-03).

BEH-MET-04.text: **Time to close.** For each configured CLOCK (any status, F03) the report gives `n`, `median`, `p90` separately (never pooled across clocks). Population = completed cycles (a start and a stop event of the clock exist for the cycle; F01 `cycle` counter); incomplete cycles are excluded and counted as `open_count`. Median: arithmetic mean of the two middle values for even n. p90: nearest-rank (ceil(0.9 x n)-th smallest). Durations in hours with the clock's `calendar_basis`. `n = 0` yields `value: null, reason: "no_completed_cycles"`, never 0.

BEH-MET-05.text: **Month-end totals.** One function `month_end_total(cutoff_ts, denominator_ref, source)` computed by one documented query on the target tables without joins that can fan out (a test asserts the query plan has no join to a many-side table; row count of the base set equals contributions). Arithmetic uses `decimal.Decimal` (money from REAL read via `Decimal(repr(x))`, quantised to the currency minor unit with ROUND_HALF_EVEN only at presentation). `cutoff_ts` and denominator are policy (CUTOFF kind) and required parameters; there is no hidden default (E-MET-CUTOFF-REQUIRED). Reference on the baseline: `SUM(cases.amount)` for all 125 cases = 622,826.44.

BEH-MET-06.text: **Unparsable amounts.** For sources holding text amounts (vendor rows, feed quantities) an unparsable value is an error object `{row_id, raw_text, code}`. By default the function raises E-MET-UNPARSABLE-INPUT listing rows; the caller may pass `allow_partial=true`, then the result is flagged `partial = true` with the error list and count and is never rendered without that flag. Nothing is skipped silently.

BEH-MET-07.text: **Reproducibility.** `reproduce(metric_value_id)` recomputes from the stored parameters and an `inputs_hash` over the inputs (event ids / row ids and content hashes) and returns equal/not-equal with a diff; a stored value that does not reproduce is reported as a defect. Each KPI has a generated documentation page (window, denominator, exclusions, tag, code reference).

BEH-MET-08.text: **Backlog ageing and unresolved-exception rate per site (R1 Should).** Parameters: `definition_tag` (required) and `as_of`. Backlog = cases not in the closing state set of the declared definition at `as_of` (state by F01 as-of); ageing buckets (<= 90, 91-365, 366-730, > 730 days) from `created_at`; per `site`. Unresolved-exception rate = open exception-queue items / all exception-queue items, per site of the matched case (unmatched items under site 'unknown'). One declared definition per table.

BEH-MET-09.text: **Cost data guard.** `operating_costs.total_cases` is never accepted as 'cases created' (E-MET-SOURCE-REFUSED); any metric using `operating_costs` has `basis = modelled` and shows it.

BEH-MET-10.text: **(R2) Unmatched rate and delay per source.** `unmatched_reference_rate` = UNMATCHED_REF + NO_BUSINESS_KEY outcomes / validated items, and `reconciliation_delay` = distribution of (`ended_at` of first run that produced an outcome minus `receipt_time`), both per source and period, from intake and run records.

BEH-MET-11.text: **(R2, Could) Case cost and rework.** Specified only as an interface placeholder: `OP-MET-05` returns E-MET-NOT-AVAILABLE until a cost input and owner exist (OPD-08).

BEH-OBS-01.text: Every request and job step emits one `http_request`/step log line with correlation id and duration; the same correlation id is on the audit record and error envelope.

BEH-OBS-02.text: Run records (F06) are the system of record for job health; the **missing-run detector** compares expected runs (when `schedule.enabled`) with `run_event`; absent runs are listed and counted.

BEH-OBS-03.text: `startup_selfcheck` logs Python, SQLite, FTS5/trigram availability, config hash, gate status (mode, holders count, schedule flag).

BEH-OBS-04.text: Latency timers wrap each operation and queue/search call; `hub report latency` (read-only) prints p50/p95 on the 125-case baseline fixture for PNFR-06. No threshold is enforced.

BEH-OBS-05.text: A KPI is "computed" when a `metric_value` row exists for each R1 KPI in the registry; `hub report kpi-coverage` lists KPIs lacking values (expected: most event-derived KPIs on the shipped baseline, with reason).

BEH-OBS-06.text: Tripwires `model_calls_total`, `egress_attempts_total`, `zone_h_service_actor_accepted` are exported at every run end; any non-zero value fails the release gate G5/G8.

BEH-OBS-07.text: Log and metric retention is hold-all until a retention policy exists (OPD-09); rotation by file size is allowed only if rotated files are kept (no deletion).

BEH-OBS-08.text: Alerts are manual in R1 (no platform): `hub report health` prints red/amber items (audit verify failing, projection mismatch, queue depth growth, missed runs, db_busy bursts, tripwires non-zero).

BEH-POL-01.text: **Policy objects** (SCH-POLICY): `policy_id`, `version` (integer, immutable once written), `kind` in {DEFINITION, CLOCK, CLOSURE, CONSISTENCY, CUTOFF}, `name`, `definition_tag` (D-OPS, D-EVID, D-FIN or other), `body` (JSON validated by kind), `owner` (string or `unassigned`), `effective_from`, `effective_to`, `status` in {candidate, adopted, accepted-open}. Editing creates a new version; old versions are never changed.

BEH-POL-02.text: **Seed content.** On a fresh install the store contains exactly three DEFINITION candidates (D-OPS 'operations marks the case closed', D-EVID 'closed and verifiable evidence and authorised approver recorded', D-FIN 'successfully resolved for cost purposes, undefined') and two CLOCK candidates (start FACT_RECEIVED; stop FACT_OPS_CLOSED or FACT_EVIDENCE_COMPLETE; `candidate_duration_hours = 48`), all `status = candidate`, `owner = unassigned`. No row has status `adopted`. Source of the candidate wording: docs/03-problem-value/success-criteria.md.

BEH-POL-03.text: **Adoption.** Transition candidate -> adopted, or recording `accepted-open` (explicit, dated, with authority_ref and reason), is Zone H ZH-05. Service, importer, scheduler actors are rejected (F02). Two adopted versions of the same (`kind`, `definition_tag`) with overlapping effective windows are refused (E-POL-OVERLAP).

BEH-POL-04.text: **Clock model.** A CLOCK body holds `clock_start_event`, `clock_stop_event`, `duration_hours` (nullable), `calendar_basis` in {wall_clock, business_calendar}, `calendar_ref` (required iff business_calendar; no calendar exists in the repo - Unknown). Elapsed time is computable under every configured clock whatever its status. A pass/fail verdict ('within 48 h') is produced only for a clock with status `adopted` and non-null `duration_hours`; otherwise the output carries `verdict: "not_available_no_adopted_policy"`.

BEH-POL-05.text: **Change events.** Every create-version, adoption, accepted-open, withdrawal, rule-row edit, rule-set activation or deactivation writes an immutable `policy_events` row `{event_id, policy_ref, actor, occurred_at, old_value, new_value, authority_ref, event_type}`; `authority_ref` must be non-empty (E-POL-AUTHORITY-REQUIRED). Edits are Zone H (ZH-10); creating a *candidate* may be done by roles quality_lead or compliance and is audited.

BEH-POL-06.text: **Rule service.** `RuleService.evaluate(ruleset_ref, function, inputs)` is a pure function of (rule-set version, inputs): no clock, randomness, I/O or database read inside the evaluation. It returns `{outcome, trace[], defaulted, defaulted_reason, ruleset_ref, authoritative}`. `trace` lists each row examined `{row_id, ordinal, matched, inputs_used}` and is sufficient to regenerate the explanation text (F08).

BEH-POL-07.text: **Rule data.** Rule rows hold thresholds, regions, effective dates, owner and default behaviour as data. The three as-found sets are loaded by a loader that reads the legacy files read-only (C11) and are marked `origin = as-found`, `read_only = true`; edits create a *custom* set, never modify an as-found one.

BEH-POL-08.text: **Active set.** Per function there is a pointer `active_ruleset`. It ships **unset**. Setting it is ZH-06. `evaluate` with an explicit `ruleset_ref` always works (read-only what-if) and returns `authoritative = false` unless that set is the active one for the function. `evaluate` without `ruleset_ref` while no active set exists returns E-POL-NO-ACTIVE-RULESET.

BEH-POL-09.text: **Defaulted marker.** If no rule row matches, or any input value is outside the declared domain of its field (unknown status, severity, region or year), the result carries `defaulted = true` and a `defaulted_reason` in {NO_MATCH_REGION_YEAR, UNKNOWN_INPUT_VALUE, NULL_INPUT}; every output that shows the result (API, pack, report, trace text) shows the marker. The as-found default **value** is preserved (999999 for AMOUNT_LIMIT; `queue` for PRIORITY fall-through) **and marked**; changing the value or replacing it by manual review requires an approved change (HAR-06) and OD-S12-04.

BEH-POL-10.text: **Divergence report (R2).** `GET /rules/divergence` runs every loaded set that publishes `amount_over_limit` over a case set or batch of inputs and lists the cases where outputs differ, with each set's trace. It resolves nothing and changes no state.

BEH-POL-11.text: **Input validation.** `amount` is parsed as `Decimal`; non-numeric, NaN or infinite input returns E-POL-INPUT-INVALID rather than an outcome (the as-found JS returned undefined behaviour for 'abc'/null - golden CT-13; behaviour change recorded in OD-S12-13).

BEH-REV-01.text: **Exception queue view** (`OP-REV-01`, HTML + JSON). Lists every item whose current outcome has a queue (quarantine_invalid, revision_review, unmatched, ambiguous_match, flagged_value): `reason_code` (primary + all), `queue`, `source`, `receipt_time`, `age` (now - receipt_time, computed at request, in hours), matched case if any, `flag_id`. Excludes `NOOP_DUPLICATE`. Filters: queue, reason, source, age >= N; default sort age descending then `raw_id`; `limit` default 50, max 100 (clamp, `next` cursor). Every quarantined/unmatched item appears in exactly one queue. Item text is shown escaped with an 'untrusted source text' marker.

BEH-REV-02.text: **Rule-trace explanation** (`OP-REV-02`): for a triage outcome (F03) the page renders a text produced by a versioned template (`trace_template`) from the stored trace fields only: rule set name+version, each examined row id, the actual input values compared, which row matched, the outcome, and the `defaulted` marker/reason if set. The same stored inputs regenerate byte-identical text. Values outside the declared domain are shown escaped. The explanation is not generated by a model and contains no advice. Each explanation shows the override/dismiss/refuse action (F02).

BEH-REV-03.text: **(R2) Search** (`OP-REV-03`). Index `doc_index` (FTS5) over documents and archive items, whole-document rows, no chunking while a document is <= configured size. Query grammar is fixed: whitespace-separated terms (implicit AND), double-quoted phrases, field filters `ref:`, `doc:`, `locale:`, `version:`, `from:` and `to:` (effective date, ISO). Maximum query length 200 characters and 12 terms; unknown field or malformed filter -> E-REV-QUERY-INVALID. User text is never passed raw to `MATCH`: every term is quoted/escaped and parameters are bound (operators `OR`, `NOT`, `NEAR`, `*`, `:` have no effect).

BEH-REV-04.text: **Search authorisation and ranking.** The `access_level` / tenant / role filter is applied inside the query before ranking and counting; totals never include denied rows. Rank = `bm25()`, ties by `effective_at` descending then `doc_id`; no reranker, no randomness. Default shows all versions with dates; `latest_only=true` collapses versions per `reference`. The trigram index is used for ja-JP and substring/ID search. NULL `ocr_confidence` is shown as 'unknown', values < 0.70 flagged, never hidden. Each hit shows doc_id, version, effective date, source, locale, access label, hash prefix, escaped `snippet()`, 'untrusted source text' marker, and the linked case if the crosswalk has one, else 'no linked case'.

BEH-REV-05.text: **No generation.** The search and queue endpoints return stored text and metadata only; no summary, answer, rewritten query, synonym expansion or recommendation exists in any response (FR-CO-04). Planted instruction strings are findable as ordinary text and are labelled; they influence nothing but text relevance.

BEH-REV-06.text: **FTS5 availability.** At start-up the product tests `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING fts5` and `trigram`; if unavailable it logs the fact, sets `search.engine = fallback` (LIKE / Python inverted index, same grammar and same result order) and reports the engine in `OP-REV-03` responses. Dev device: SQLite 3.37.2 with FTS5 + trigram verified; target runtime is Unknown (OD-S12-12).

BEH-REV-07.text: **(R2, Could) Template form.** `OP-REV-04` serves a structured form for deviation/CAPA narrative fields (labels, field types, length limits) and stores drafts owned by the author. The product never pre-fills narrative content from rules, search or intake; submission/signature of the final record happens outside the product (T4); the draft carries no Zone H power. Deferred by default (candidate for Rejected at FINAL if no stakeholder asks).

BEH-REV-08.text: **Latency measurement.** Queue and search calls emit duration timers (F-observability) so p50/p95 on the 125-case baseline can be reported (PNFR-06, target Unknown - OPD-14).

BEH-RUN-02.text: **Schedule disabled by default.** The schedule is a documented OS-level entry outside the repository calling `hub run <job> --trigger scheduled`. A `scheduled` trigger is accepted only while `schedule.enabled = true`; enabling or disabling is Zone H ZH-09 (audited event with authority_ref). While false: E-RUN-SCHEDULE-DISABLED, a run record with `outcome = refused` is still written. The question whether this is an 'automated action' under HAR-10 is OD-S12-10; both states (disabled-manual-only; enabled-non-Zone-H-jobs-only) are specified and tested.

BEH-RUN-03.text: **Run record** (SCH-RUN-RECORD). Append-only events RUN_STARTED (written before any work), RUN_CHECKPOINT, RUN_FINISHED or RUN_FAILED. Final fields: `run_id`, `job`, `trigger`, `triggered_by`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `inputs_seen`, `outcomes_by_type` (counts per reason/outcome), `errors[]`, `limit_reached` (bool), `batch_size`, `backlog_remaining`, `checkpoint`, `config_version`, `code_version`. A run that dies leaves RUN_STARTED with a stale heartbeat; the next invocation writes RUN_ABANDONED for it.

BEH-RUN-04.text: **Totals reconcile.** `sum(outcomes_by_type)` equals the count of `intake_outcome` rows carrying that `run_id`; a mismatch fails the run (E-RUN-TOTALS-MISMATCH) and is reported.

BEH-RUN-05.text: **No silent cap.** A capacity limit (`batch_size`, default configured explicitly, no hidden constant) may stop a run early; then `limit_reached = true`, `backlog_remaining` = exact count of unprocessed eligible items, and the checkpoint stores the ordering key (`receipt_time, raw_id`) of the last processed item. The next run resumes from the checkpoint. With `--until-empty` the job loops until `backlog_remaining = 0`.

BEH-RUN-06.text: **Single flight.** One active run per job: a lock row with heartbeat (default stale after 15 min, configurable). A second start returns E-RUN-ALREADY-RUNNING and writes a refused run record.

BEH-RUN-07.text: **Idempotent resume.** Killing a run at any point and re-running yields the same final store as an uninterrupted run (no duplicate effects), because intake outcomes are keyed by (`raw_id`, stage) and skipped when present.

BEH-RUN-08.text: **Missing-run detector.** When `schedule.enabled = true` the detector lists expected-but-absent runs (expected times from configuration); with schedule disabled it reports 'schedule disabled' instead of failures.

BEH-RUN-09.text: **Timeliness record.** Each run records `ended_at`; the report 'finished before 06:00 local business time' uses configuration `site.timezone` (Unknown; default UTC labelled as such) so PNFR-02 is measurable once a schedule exists.

BEH-SEC-01.text: **Authenticate everything.** Every route except `GET /healthz` (liveness only, no data) and `POST /auth/login` requires authentication; unauthenticated requests get 401 `E-AUTH-UNAUTHENTICATED`. A route registry test enumerates all registered routes and fails if any route lacks a declared permission (deny by default).

BEH-SEC-02.text: **Local authenticator (stopgap, behind the `Authenticator` interface).** Users stored with salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (`hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac`, per-user 16-byte salt, iterations configurable, proposed >= 600,000), constant-time comparison (`hmac.compare_digest`), password length >= 12. Sessions: 256-bit random token (`secrets`), only its SHA-256 stored server-side; idle expiry 30 min, absolute 8 h (proposals); cookie `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` (+`Secure` under TLS). Lockout: 5 failed logins per user in 15 min lock the account 15 min; failure responses are generic. No default or bootstrap account; users are created offline by the host operator with `hub user create` (no web bootstrap).

BEH-SEC-03.text: **Service identities.** Service accounts (`principal_kind = service`, recorded as `actor_kind = system` in decision events and `service` in the audit log) authenticate with bearer tokens (stored hashed, rotatable), cannot start interactive sessions, and are rejected for every Zone H action and human-link action (F02, F05). Scheduler/importer runs use a service identity.

BEH-SEC-04.text: **Roles and permissions.** Roles: reviewer, quality_lead, compliance, finance_read, integration, dispositioner. The permission matrix (security-spec.md SEC-MATRIX) is data; a request needs an explicit permission for its operation, otherwise 403 `E-AUTH-FORBIDDEN`. finance_read is read-only with masked identifiers; integration is non-human and limited to intake/run operations; `dispositioner` alone does not grant Zone H (the holder list also must contain the principal).

BEH-SEC-05.text: **Audit chain.** Every decision event, policy/rule change, Zone H attempt (accepted or rejected), authorisation failure, login success/failure, lockout, configuration load, export, read of C3 data, audit verification and schedule change appends an `audit_log` record (SCH-AUDIT): `audit_seq`, `occurred_at`, `actor`, `actor_kind`, `action`, `object_ref`, `outcome` in {success, denied, error}, `reason` (non-empty for C3 reads and exports), `correlation_id`, `details` (canonical JSON), `prev_hash`, `hash = sha256(prev_hash ‖ canonical(record))`. Canonical form: JSON with sorted keys, `separators=(",", ":")`, `ensure_ascii=true`, UTC timestamps `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ`. The audit write is in the same transaction as the change it records; failure aborts the change. Audit rows are insert-only (trigger).

BEH-SEC-06.text: **Anchor and verify.** The head `{audit_seq, hash, occurred_at}` is appended to an anchor file at `audit.anchor_path` (outside the database directory) every `audit.anchor_every` records (proposed 100) and at the end of every run; `hub verify-audit` recomputes the chain from the first record, checks each anchored head against the chain, and reports `ok` or the first broken `audit_seq` with the failure kind (altered record, missing record, reordered, head mismatch). Verification is a release gate (CO-03). Truncation of records after the last anchor is not detectable (documented residual risk).

BEH-SEC-07.text: **No secrets in the repository or logs.** Secrets only via environment; a secret-scan gate has 0 findings; logs and audit `details` never contain passwords, tokens or hashes of credentials.

BEH-SEC-08.text: **Transport.** Default bind is 127.0.0.1. A non-loopback bind requires `network.exposure_approved = true` (HAR-05 evidence reference in config) and TLS settings; otherwise start-up is refused (E-SEC-EXPOSURE-NOT-APPROVED). No outbound network calls except the loopback gateway reader (component rule 7).

BEH-SEC-09.text: **Web protections.** State-changing HTML forms carry a per-session CSRF token (E-SEC-CSRF); JSON writes require a custom header `X-Hub-Request: 1` plus SameSite cookie or bearer token; all output is HTML-escaped; `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` are set; request body limit (default 1 MiB) and `414/413` handling as in legacy (page size clamps).

BEH-SEC-10.text: **(R2) Data protection by field class.** Classes C1-C3 and the per-field handling of metadata-model M3 are enforced: finance_read sees `account_id` masked; `restricted` documents and legal-hold data need a named role; missing `access_level`/`classification` = `restricted`; every C3 read and export writes an audit record with a non-empty `reason` (E-SEC-REASON-REQUIRED). Tenant filters are mandatory in queries.

BEH-SEC-11.text: **Retention hold.** No code path deletes cases, events, evidence, audit rows or intake rows (PNFR-10, OD-S12-09); a test greps for `DELETE FROM` against those tables and verifies triggers.

BR-01.text: Every reported case figure (closed, resolved, cost, handling time) shall declare which definition of the state it uses, and figures built on different definitions shall not be combined or compared.

BR-02.text: The organisation shall record who decides the definition of closed/resolved and the closure-time expectation. The engagement shall not choose it.

BR-03.text: Time-to-close shall be measurable under each candidate definition (elapsed from receipt to ops-closed, and to evidence-complete) without prejudging which is correct.

BR-04.text: Externally received case information shall be matched to exactly one core case, or flagged unmatched, before it reaches a reviewer's queue.

BR-05.text: A re-delivered or replayed item shall not increase the exception queue or alter totals.

BR-06.text: Delayed, missing or revised items shall be detectable and attributable to a source and time without manual spreadsheet reconciliation.

BR-07.text: Each case decision shall carry the evidence relied on and its source, retrievable on request.

BR-08.text: Batch disposition and any other decision requiring an authorised person shall remain a human decision; no process shall make, pre-fill as final, or simulate it.

BR-09.text: No case shall be closed without verifiable evidence unless an owner has explicitly authorised an exception rule.

BR-10.text: Case cost and avoidable rework shall be attributable per case and per period using one agreed cut-off and denominator.

BR-11.text: Existing legitimate workflows (including the parallel path for older customers) shall not be disrupted without an identified owner's agreement.

BR-12.text: Backlog ageing and unresolved exception rate shall be visible per site and comparable across sites.

BR-13.text: Change to the handling process shall be releasable without causing a rollback of the kind documented in 2025.

FR-GATE-03.text: Transitions classified as Zone H (disposition, release, e-signature, closure of a case failing the evidence rule, adoption of a definition or rule, acceptance of an exception rule) SHALL be accepted only from an authenticated human actor holding a configured authorised role; scheduler, importer and service accounts SHALL be rejected.

FR-GATE-04.text: The authorised-role holder list SHALL be configuration and SHALL ship empty; until at least one holder is configured, Zone H transitions SHALL be unavailable. No default holder SHALL be created.
FR-GATE-04.verification: Fresh install: Zone H transitions refused until holder configured

FR-GATE-05.text: The recording mode of a disposition SHALL be a configuration choice: (a) record the human's decision as an event in this system, or (b) record only a reference to the decision held in an external system of record. The system SHALL NOT assume either; the choice is open (OPD-05).
FR-GATE-05.verification: Both modes exercised in test; default mode = none (blocked) until configured

FR-GATE-06.text: A reviewer SHALL be able to override, dismiss or refuse any rule-generated flag, classification or priority, with a reason recorded; the override SHALL never be blocked by the system.
FR-GATE-06.verification: Every rule output has an override action; override produces an event

FR-ID-01.text: The system SHALL maintain an explicit crosswalk linking case, batch, deviation, CAPA and feed reference, each link recording key used, creator (rule or human) and time.
FR-ID-01.verification: Every link has key + creator + time; lookup by any id returns linked set

FR-ID-02.text: Orphans SHALL remain orphans: no link SHALL be created by guessing or similarity. A human MAY create a link; that is recorded as an event.

FR-ID-03.text: The system SHALL surface, as findings and without auto-correction, cross-object state combinations that a configured consistency rule marks contradictory (e.g. a case closed while a linked batch is on hold). The rule set is policy (RC-3); none ships adopted.

FR-ID-04.text: A read-only joined view SHALL let an investigator see all linked objects for any identifier (touchpoint T5, deterministic).

FR-INT-02.text: Re-delivery of an item whose content is identical to one already processed SHALL change neither the exception queue nor any total.

RC-1.text: The step that records a case decision, closure or batch disposition (with actor and basis) has no representation in the system. The only writer of `cases` is the data generator (`app/generate.py:37`); the API is GET-only (`app/server.py`)

RC-2.text: Case state is a mutable snapshot: `cases.version` = 1 for 125/125 with no code that increments it; creation event stores the *current* status (125/125); only 2 event types exist; 8 REOPENED cases have 0 reopen events

RC-3.text: No owned definition of "closed / resolved / approved", and no decider for the speed-vs-evidence trade-off (DR-20, DR-21, DR-23 are GAPs; `operations-vs-risk-2024.md`: "never formalized")

RC-4.text: The approval/priority logic exists as three unsynchronised implementations: `app/legacy_logic.py` (>50,000), `legacy_js/legacy_policy.js` (regional limit x 1.05, default 999,999), `legacy_batch/shift_reconciliation.py` (threshold 2,500-8,500); the Java/SQL month-end paths do not call the Python rule despite the header comment

RC-5.text: Execution is manual-start, capacity-capped and unrecorded: no scheduler anywhere; `reconcile(limit=1000)` vs 8,567 backlog rows (9 runs); reconcile writes no run record

RC-6.text: Intake is destructive and content-blind: reconcile overwrites `processing_status` in place; every REPLAY becomes DUPLICATE without content comparison; invalid gateway events are counted, not stored; `source-contract-v1.json` is not enforced; Java skips unparsable amounts

RC-7.text: No shared identity or referential model: `cases` has no batch/deviation/CAPA/feed key; `partner_feeds.ref_id` has no FK; five status vocabularies; no constraint across case/batch/deviation/CAPA/lab states

RC-8.text: Month-end figures are computed independently without a shared definition: SQL `LEFT JOIN events` inflates `SUM(amount)` by 19.3% on the shipped data (742,956.61 vs 622,826.44, re-executed read-only); Java `double` with silent `NumberFormatException` skip; API counts

SBR-CO-01.text: A difference from a Stage 7 golden is acceptable only if it is in the deviation register with status `approved` and an approval reference (HAR-06).

SBR-CO-02.text: Executable acceptance runs only in a full repo copy outside the working tree (OD-03a), with manifest verification after.

SBR-CO-03.text: No AI, LLM or ML call or dependency; no model-inference egress.

SBR-DEC-01.text: `decision_events` rows are insert-only. `seq` per case is gapless from 1. Corrections are new events referencing the corrected `event_id`; no event is ever altered or removed.

SBR-DEC-02.text: `recorded_at` is server UTC and not client-settable. `occurred_at <= recorded_at` and `occurred_at >= occurred_at` of the previous event of the same case.

SBR-DEC-03.text: **Closing-state set.** (a) If a CLOSURE policy is active (selected by ZH-05 and status adopted or accepted-open) the closing set is `body.closing_states` of that policy. (b) If none is active, behaviour follows `closure.unconfigured_behaviour`: `treat_label_CLOSED_as_closing` (**default**; every transition into a state whose vocabulary role tag is `closing_label` is checked, fail-closed) or `none` (no check; events flagged `closure_check = not_configured`). The choice of (b) value is Zone H configuration (ZH-08-class) and is open decision OD-S12-03.

SBR-DEC-04.text: A closing transition requires >= 1 `evidence_ref` that resolves to an existing evidence record **or** an accepted `close_exception` (Zone H). Sufficiency is never evaluated; it is policy (OPD-07, OD-S12-07).

SBR-DEC-05.text: Imported legacy REOPENED cases without a reopen event carry the marker `LEGACY_UNEVIDENCED_REOPEN`; the invariant 'no REOPENED case without a REOPEN event' is evaluated on non-marked cases and the marked ones are listed. No reopen event is invented.

SBR-DEC-06.text: A REOPEN event increments `cycle`; the three fact events (FACT_RECEIVED, FACT_OPS_CLOSED, FACT_EVIDENCE_COMPLETE) belong to a cycle. Elapsed time under a clock is computed per completed cycle.

SBR-DEC-07.text: Transition legality: `structural` mode permits any change between two distinct states of the case vocabulary except Zone H ones; a strict table may replace it (OD-S12-16). Vocabularies are never mapped to each other.

SBR-GATE-01.text: The Zone H action list ZH-01..ZH-10 is closed. An action outside the list cannot be accepted (E-GATE-UNKNOWN-ACTION).

SBR-GATE-02.text: A Zone H action is accepted iff: interactive human session AND principal in `zone_h.holders` AND role dispositioner AND re-authentication within `zone_h.reauth_window_seconds` AND mode/values permit the action AND `pack_hash` current (for ZH-01..03). Any other combination is rejected and audited. No setting disables a condition.

SBR-GATE-03.text: Disposition recording follows `disposition.mode` in {none (default), event, external_ref}; the mode in force at write time is stored on the event; past events are never rewritten.

SBR-GATE-04.text: Override, dismiss or refuse of any rule-generated item is always accepted from an authenticated reviewer-class role when a non-empty reason is supplied; the original output is retained.

SBR-GATE-05.text: Inbound text, rule output, report content, search results and template content never populate a disposition value or trigger a Zone H event.

SBR-ID-01.text: Rule links only by registered exact key; no similarity of any kind.

SBR-ID-02.text: Orphan counts are reported measures; orphans are never repaired by the product.

SBR-ID-03.text: A human link needs a registered pair, a reason and an authenticated human reviewer-class role; it is an event.

SBR-INT-01.text: **Item identity.** `identity_key = sha256(canonical([source, partner, record_kind, ref_id, source_ts]))`. `business_key` and `feed_id` are not identities (FND-INT-2). Identity-key definition per source is configuration; the feed definition is OD-S12-17.

SBR-INT-02.text: `content_hash = sha256(canonical({schema_rev, payload}))`, canonical = UTF-8, sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace; transport fields excluded.

SBR-INT-03.text: **Reason precedence** (highest first): UNSUPPORTED_REVISION, INVALID_JSON, MISSING_ENVELOPE_FIELD, UNKNOWN_RECORD_KIND, MISSING_PAYLOAD_FIELD, CONTRACT_VIOLATION (enforce only), REVISED_CONFLICT, UNPARSABLE_AMOUNT, NO_BUSINESS_KEY, AMBIGUOUS_MATCH, UNMATCHED_REF, NEGATIVE_VALUE, UNKNOWN_UNIT, UNKNOWN_CURRENCY, IDENTIFIER_PATTERN. The first applicable is `primary_reason`; all applicable are in `all_reasons`.

SBR-INT-04.text: Order of stages: store raw -> identity/hash comparison (NOOP or conflict) -> validate -> classify -> match -> outcome. A conflict still records validation results in `all_reasons`.

SBR-INT-05.text: Matching is exact string equality (NFC + trim) on registered keys; 0 hits -> UNMATCHED_REF, 1 -> link, >1 -> AMBIGUOUS_MATCH.

SBR-INT-06.text: Untrusted text never reaches decision parameters; payload `state`/`quality_flag`/`subtype` are stored as source attributes only.

SBR-INT-07.text: Contract binding default is `record_only` for every source; `enforce` is per-source configuration (OD-S12-11).

SBR-INT-08.text: Duplicates (`NOOP_DUPLICATE`) are excluded from every queue, total and metric by definition of the outcome views.

SBR-MET-01.text: A metric involving closed, resolved, approved, cost or handling time must name a `definition_tag`.

SBR-MET-02.text: Values with different tags or tag-policy versions are never summed, averaged or compared.

SBR-MET-03.text: Median = mean of middle two for even n; p90 = nearest-rank ceil(0.9 n); n=0 gives null.

SBR-MET-04.text: Money is `Decimal`; no float arithmetic; rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) only at presentation.

SBR-MET-05.text: An unparsable amount is an error, never skipped; partial results are flagged.

SBR-MET-06.text: Every KPI output carries window, denominator, exclusions, tag and 'synthetic, unvalidated' while data are synthetic.

SBR-POL-01.text: Policy object versions and rule rows are immutable; change = new version; each change is a `policy_events` row with old value, new value, actor, time and a non-empty `authority_ref`.

SBR-POL-02.text: The shipped product contains no policy object with status `adopted`, no active rule set, no `disposition.mode` other than `none`, no holder, and no enabled schedule.

SBR-POL-03.text: `evaluate()` is pure: output = f(rule-set version, inputs).

SBR-POL-04.text: **Defaulted marker.** An outcome carries `defaulted = true` if no row matches or an input is outside the field's declared domain; the as-found default value is retained and marked until a decision under OPD-04 / HAR-06 says otherwise.

SBR-POL-05.text: As-found rule sets are read-only; custom sets are separate objects.

SBR-POL-06.text: A pass/fail verdict on a clock exists only when the clock is `adopted` and `duration_hours` is set; otherwise only elapsed times are reported.

SBR-POL-07.text: Adopted versions of the same (`kind`, `definition_tag`) cannot have overlapping effective windows.

SBR-POL-08.text: Boundary convention for a duration check: within the clock iff `elapsed <= duration` (inclusive) in the clock's calendar basis. [Assumption; owner of the clock may change it as policy.]

SBR-RUN-01.text: No hidden capacity cap: every limit is configuration, printed in the run record; remaining work is counted and checkpointed.

SBR-RUN-02.text: One active run per job; a dead run is closed by RUN_ABANDONED.

SBR-RUN-03.text: Jobs never perform Zone H actions.

SBR-SEC-01.text: Deny by default for routes, fields, roles and unknown access levels.

SBR-SEC-02.text: Audit record is written in the same transaction as the audited change; failure aborts the change.

SBR-SEC-03.text: Hold-all: no delete path for retained tables until a retention policy is adopted (OPD-09).
